subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed `sessions_spawn` startup failures be solved as a new lifecycle/progress contract, as a narrower sandbox fail-start terminalization/logging fix, or only after live Docker proof narrows the root cause?
rationale: The remaining work crosses supported sandbox defaults, accepted child-run semantics, session state projection, and the overlapping but unmerged lifecycle design, so automation should not pick the permanent contract without maintainer intent and live proof.

options.title: Require live proof, then choose contract
options.body: Keep this issue open, require a current-main Docker-backed `non-main` repro, and then decide whether the fix belongs in lifecycle phases, sandbox startup handling, or both.

options.title: Fold into lifecycle tracker
options.body: Treat the sandbox symptom as covered by the broader startup-silence contract at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 and close this only if maintainers accept that tracker as canonical for Docker startup failures too.

options.title: Queue narrow sandbox repair
options.body: Sponsor a focused repair that forces Docker create/start failures into child session terminal state and logs, while leaving the broader `first-progress`/`startup-failed` API decision separate.

recommendation.title: Require live proof, then choose contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, require a current-main Docker-backed `non-main` repro, and then decide whether the fix belongs in lifecycle phases, sandbox startup handling, or both.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame points to their recent refactor across the central child-runtime and lifecycle projection lines, making them the best available routing candidate for the contract decision.
